A seat is one coupe boundary on the timber licence, drawn on a 1:2000 survey and stamped with a brand die cut for that operator. The die face is filed as a photo, its notches and dents its own, so a recut die struck on bark the colour of crushed velvet leaves another scar. Every log takes that brand on the butt, shot again at the mill gate.

Fifty clones need fifty coupes: survey 6,000, licence 34,000, yard scale 12,000, 20,000 seedlings from the replant garden, 2.2 million dollars before one trunk rolls. Two firs leave the saw alike; the brand names which coupe they stood in.
